_README: A LANE PRESET: what a search is looking for and what it is not.
Copied to config/lane-vocab.json by `node setup.mjs`, then yours to edit.
Underscore sections are read by one consumer each (named in `_comment`); every other
top-level key is a shared anti-lane FAMILY that both title scorers read, with one weight
per scorer because each penalty is sized against the bonus it answers.
Patterns in shared families and `_ranker` must be valid in BOTH JavaScript and Python.

_preset.name: techart-ai-tooling
_preset.description: Senior technical art (rigging, pipeline, tools, digital humans) plus AI tooling, agentic and evaluation engineering. The tuning this fork was built with.

terms: applied AI|applied research|AI engineer|ML engineer|machine learning|\bMLOps\b|AI\/ML

_ranker._comment: Read by pipeline-audit.mjs --rank. JavaScript regex, case-insensitive. `lanes` add their weight per matching term; `deprioritised` and `managerial` subtract; `out_of_lane` is an outright -99; `ic_director` exempts IC director titles from the managerial penalty.

_lane._comment: Read by scripts/_lane.py (board sweeps). Python regex, case-insensitive.

_assist._comment: Read by scripts/eval-assist.py. Python regex, case-insensitive.
gates: \b(ph\.?d\.?|master'?s degree|ms or phd|advanced degree)\b[^.]{0,60}\b(required|must have|is a requirement)\b|\brequire[sd]?\b[^.]{0,40}\b(ph\.?d\.?|master'?s)\b

_role_gate.pattern: \b(developer advocate|developer relations|devrel|developer experience|technical marketing|solutions engineer|solutions architect|forward deployed|sales engineer|customer engineer|field engineer|evangelist|content workflow)\b
_role_gate._comment: Read by score-model.mjs. Titles this search de-prioritises: a matching title keeps only 25% of its company preference. Omit to disable the gate.

_board._comment: Read by the board builders. Each role goes to the FIRST lane whose words appear in ' <lowercased title> '; `cv` is the CV variant the dashboard suggests; lanes with a `button` get a filter button on the boards.

_title_filter._comment: Written into portals.yml title_filter by setup.mjs. Substring match, case-insensitive; at least one positive and no negative must match.

why: 'Agent' in a title is not always an AI agent. At a marketplace or any consumer
company it usually means a HUMAN support agent, and the lane bonus then ranks
customer service above the actual AI work. Sweeping Whatnot put 'Trust & Safety
Agent' and seven 'Customer Experience Agent' rows above its own AI Tooling Engineer
and LLM Platform Engineer: 11 of 19 triage rows, 58% of the output, all sitting
above the roles the sweep existed to find.
These outweigh the agent bonus deliberately. Ranking the anti-lane FIRST is worse
than ranking nothing, because the top of the list is the entry a human reads. It
costs a genuine title now and then, an AI lab's 'Trust & Safety' ML req being the
likeliest, and both scorers accept that trade.
The list is open-ended by nature, since a consumer company can put 'Agent' after
almost any operations noun. Enumerating them is the stopgap that TITLE-ONLY triage
allows; scoring the body is the real answer wherever a body exists.
'Test & Evaluation' is a defence-industry discipline, verifying that a weapon system
meets its spec, not LLM evaluation. It collects the full eval bonus and once put
a cluster of defence-industry T&E reqs high on a candidate list. The profile's eval
specialty is agent and model quality, which shares a word with this and nothing else.
An absolute disqualifier for a senior candidate, and these reqs score WELL on lane
keywords because the research topics sit right on the profile's subject matter:
'NVIDIA 2027 Internships: Ph.D. Research Graphics and Simulation' scored 7 and
reached the top of a large pending-req list.
Two boundary bugs have already been paid for here and both are pinned by cases.
`interns?` does not match 'Internships', because there is no word boundary inside
the word, so the plural form scored POSITIVE. And `new ?grad` does not match 'New
College Grad', which is the spelling NVIDIA uses.
This profile targets an IC AI/ML ENGINEER title, not product or programme
leadership, and these reqs surface at the top of triage purely because 'agentic'
appears in their titles. NVIDIA's 'Technical Program Manager - Local AI Agents' is
the case that forced programme manager in here: _lane.py had it, the ranker's copy
covered only product manager, and the req ranked with the engineering roles.
Manager-of-engineers is deliberately NOT matched. That is a different question from
product management, and the ranker answers it separately with its own managerial
rule plus the craft-director exemption, because in games and VFX a 'Technical
Director' is a senior individual contributor, not a people manager.
patterns: \b(product manager|product management|program manager|programme manager|project manager|technical program manager|\bTPM\b|\bPM\b)\b

why: GPU kernel and compiler work is a hard anti-lane in this profile, and it wears agentic vocabulary
at NVIDIA: 'Senior System Software Engineer, Agentic Kernel Development' ranked with
the real agentic reqs in the 2026-09-20 triage. _lane.py has penalised this since it
was written and the Node ranker scored it POSITIVELY, which is the same hand-port gap
the rest of this file exists to close.
Note a real disagreement that is NOT here: `inference`. _lane.py penalises it as a
documented gap area and the ranker rewards it. That is a judgement about two
different jobs (serving infrastructure against applied AI) and it stays local to each
file rather than being averaged away.
Chip design, one step further out than kernel work and weighted harder in both
scorers for the same reason: no amount of lane vocabulary in the title makes a
physical-design req applicable. Ported verbatim from _lane.py's LANE_DOWN so that
file's behaviour is unchanged and only the ranker gains the rule.
The family whose drift started all of this. This profile de-prioritises customer-
facing and pre-sales titles in favour of an IC AI/ML ENGINEER title, and both scorers
agreed on that, separately, in two spellings. _lane.py wrote
`solutions? (architect|engineer)`; the ranker wrote the PLURAL only. NVIDIA writes
'Solution Architect' singular, so three of them led a 593-req triage.
'Technical marketing' is deliberately NOT here, and the two scorers genuinely
disagree about it: the ranker de-prioritises it while _lane.py scores it POSITIVELY,
because in this profile Technical Marketing Engineer is a target title rather than a
customer-facing one. That disagreement is a real judgement, not drift, so it stays
local to each file rather than being averaged away here.
patterns: \b(solutions? (architect|engineer)|sales engineer|customer engineer|field engineer|forward deployed|adoption architect|customer success|account executive|evangelist|developer (advocate|relations)|devrel)\b

why: Added from a 593-req inbox backlog. 'Agentic identity' is an infosec specialty and
the word agent carries the whole lane bonus: NVIDIA's 'Principal Cyber Security
Engineer - Agentic Identity and Security', 'Staff Security Engineer - PAM and Agentic
Identity' and Databricks' 'Staff Security Software Engineer, Agentic Security
Engineering' all tied at the top of triage with the real agentic reqs.
Matched on security-specific NOUNS rather than on the word 'safety', because AI
safety is a wanted lane in this profile and _lane.py scores it positively. A
security-automation req whose title scored 0 is the standing proof that a security
TITLE can hide real agentic work, which is why this is a weighted penalty and not a
disqualifier: its body rescued it to 4.64.
patterns: \b(cyber ?security|information security|infosec|application security|security operations|\bSOC\b|privileged access|\bPAM\b|identity and access|\bIAM\b|threat (detection|intelligence|modell?ing)|incident response|vulnerability management|penetration test)\b

why: Site reliability and network operations are infrastructure duty, not this profile's lane, and
they attract tooling vocabulary: NVIDIA's 'Senior AI Tools Engineer, SRE Operations
- GeForce NOW' scored as highly as the agentic reqs on 'AI Tools' plus 'Tools
Engineer' alone. Weighted lighter than the other families here on purpose. Tooling
FOR an ops team is still tooling, and the intent is to move it off the top of the
list rather than bury it. MLOps is untouched, since that is a wanted lane in this profile.
patterns: \b(site reliability|\bSRE\b|network operations|\bNOC\b|IT operations|help ?desk|service desk|on-?call rotation engineer)\b

why: Billable delivery work against someone else's roadmap, and customer-facing, which
this profile de-prioritises. Salesforce's 'Agentic Operations Consultant' reached the
top of triage on the agent bonus with nothing in either scorer to answer it.
Policy and standards-body work reads as agentic vocabulary and is not engineering.
OpenAI's 'Agent Standards Specialist, Global Affairs' ranked with the engineering
reqs. 'Standards' on its own is not matched, because standards work on OpenUSD and
AOUSD is squarely this profile's lane; the government and policy nouns are what separate them.
patterns: \b(global affairs|public policy|government affairs|policy (manager|lead|analyst|specialist)|regulatory affairs|trust and safety policy)\b

_triage._comment: Read by scripts/triage-leads.py. [label, Python regex]: a pasted lead whose title matches is set aside with that label (still printed, never silently dropped).
gates: \b(forward[- ]deployed|forward[- ]deployment|solutions? engineer|solution engineer|solutions? architect|deployment (strategist|engineer)|consultant|developer advocate|advocate|technical architect|architect lead|ai architect|ai builder|go[- ]to[- ]market|gtm|growth marketing|enterprise solutions|field engineer|customer engineer|sales engineer|account|professional services)\b

_sweep._comment: Read by scripts/nvidia-sweep.py: the search terms it sends to NVIDIA's board. With none, it falls back to the title filter's positives.
